title: Culper Research Alleges Cerebras Chips Fail Within 2 Years in New Short Report
summary:
The short-selling firm Culper Research has taken a position against AI hardware maker Cerebras, arguing that the company's core wafer-scale engine technology is prone to premature breakdown. In a report released Tuesday, the firm alleged that Cerebras's chips break down after roughly 1.5 to 2.5 years in the field, a lifespan that it claims would cause the expensive hardware to depreciate rapidly and undermine the company's business model.

Culper further claimed that Cerebras uses a workaround of "dummy operations" to prevent the chips from cooling and breaking, which in turn accelerates wear. The report also challenged the company's claims regarding its connector materials, alleging the use of a pre-existing product called PariPoser from Paricon Technologies. Shares of Cerebras fell about 5% following the announcement.

selectedTweets.text:
A very sharp friend of mine sent me a take arguing that Cerebras chips could depreciate extremely quickly. I thought I’d share it here.

Cerebras’ wafer-scale engine (WSE) and routing architecture do seem fully capable of solving the yield problem, as the company claims. The uncertainty is around how long the wafer will actually last in operation.

Cerebras’ design requires a large number of redundant interconnects to accommodate manufacturing defects. But all that BEOL wiring significantly increases the effective area susceptible to TDDB (time-dependent dielectric breakdown), potentially creating much greater long-term reliability risks. TDDB can cause shorts, which are more dangerous than opens in this design.

Dielectric thickness determines the probability of TDDB, and variations in that thickness can be spatially correlated across a wafer. That makes it highly likely that many interconnect failures would cluster in a particular region. It is unclear how Cerebras detects these shorts and avoids using the failed interconnects.

Ultimately, the argument is that you have a design that is expensive to begin with and also ages extremely quickly.
